item.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial puts spotlight on treatment for severe mental illness
item.description: The defense in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial called multiple witnesses Tuesday. Clancy has admitted to killing her three young children in 2023, but has pleaded not guilty to murder, arguing she had postpartum psychosis, bipolar disorder and was being overmedicated. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: NASA images show 60-foot-wide crater on moon after SpaceX rocket booster crash
item.description: A NASA spacecraft circling the moon is providing the sharpest views yet of the crater carved by a crashing SpaceX rocket.

item.title: Trump says no talks with Iran ongoing, and none scheduled
item.description: President Trump says the U.S. is not engaged in any talks with Iran as the two countries remain locked in a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz after almost six months of war.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy said a voice ordered her to kill children, psychologist testifies
item.description: A psychologist who met with Lindsay Clancy in the hospital after her children's deaths testified Tuesday at her Massachusetts murder trial.

item.title: Where things stand in Iran as White House sends mixed messages on U.S.-Iran communications
item.description: President Trump took to social media on Tuesday to say there are no ongoing or planned talks with Iran aimed toward ending the war. CBS News' Nancy Cordes reports on the latest developments and Aaron David Miller, senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, joins with analysis.

item.title: From 2024: Tommy John on Tommy John surgery, before and after
item.description: In this interview from 2024, former pitching ace Tommy John talked with correspondent Faith Salie about the injury to his pitching arm he suffered in 1974, and about the innovative procedure (which came to be known as "Tommy John surgery") that rescued his career – and would prolong the careers of many more professional and amateur athletes since. [John died on Aug. 15, 2026 at age 83.]

item.title: From 1981: Yankees pitcher Tommy John
item.description: Pitcher Tommy John, who in the 1970s underwent an innovative procedure on his injured pitching arm that would become famous as "Tommy John surgery," died on Aug. 15, 2026 at age 83. In this "Sunday Morning" story that aired Aug. 16, 1981, John talked with correspondent Heywood Hale Broun about his comeback after surgery, and about baseball's other comeback – returning to the field following the major league players' nearly two-month-long strike. [Also appearing are Yankee outfielder Lou Pinella and trainer Gene Monahan.]

item.title: Ukraine targets Moscow with drones as Russia threatens U.K. over support
item.description: Ukraine targets Moscow with a huge wave of drones as Russia warns the U.K. will pay a price for supplying Kyiv with long-range weapons.

item.title: Inside Alaska's nonpartisan primary for Senate
item.description: A primary is underway in Alaska on Tuesday for an open Senate seat. CBS News' Anthony Salvanto takes a look at the state's unique primary system.

item.title: Florida voters choose in governor, Senate primaries, and more races to watch
item.description: Three states are holding primaries on Tuesday, with Florida deciding on nominees for both governor and for Senate.

item.title: Justice Department to send a record 1,000 monitors to midterm polling places
item.description: The Justice Department is planning to deploy a record 1,000 federal monitors to polling places throughout the U.S. for the midterm elections.

item.title: What to know as Florida holds primaries for governor, U.S. Senate and U.S. House
item.description: Florida is holding primary elections Tuesday with races for governor and both chambers of Congress. CBS News contributor Marc Caputo breaks down the contests and CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto has a look at the national implications.

item.title: Frank Beard, ZZ Top drummer, dies at age 77
item.description: "Today, Elwood and I lost a great friend and collaborator, and the world lost one of the most naturally innovative drummers and a great and true son of Texas," ZZ Top's Billy Gibbons said in a statement.

item.title: Beagles bred for research get new life amid questions over federal oversight
item.description: The USDA's own inspector general has repeatedly raised concerns about federal oversight of dog breeders.

item.title: Landmark social media trial against Meta underway
item.description: New York Times technology reporter Mike Isaac joins CBS News to break down the landmark social media trial against Meta that's currently underway, with parents accusing the tech giant of designing its platforms to be addictive and harmful to children.

item.title: Tupac Shakur autopsy photos shown at murder trial after some family members leave
item.description: Tupac Shakur's cousin said the autopsy photos made him feel "very angry, to say the least."

item.title: U.S. quietly deporting Mexican migrants to Guatemala and Honduras
item.description: The Trump administration has been quietly deporting migrants from Mexico to different countries in Central America despite the Mexican government's willingness to accept the return of all its citizens, two Department of Homeland Security officials told CBS News. CBS News immigration correspondent Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more.

item.title: Meta's federal trial begins over child social media addiction claims
item.description: The lawsuit accuses the social media giant of contributing to the youth mental health crisis by deliberately designing features that addict children to its platforms.

item.title: Who is Natalie Harp? Trump's loyal assistant suddenly in the spotlight
item.description: The 35-year-old executive assistant to the president is a quiet but loyal force at President Trump's side.

item.title: Former NIAID adviser pleads guilty in COVID-19 records scheme
item.description: David Morens, 78, agreed to plead guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit offenses and to defraud the United States.

item.title: Inflation is outpacing wages again. Many workers were already behind.
item.description: When inflation rises faster than workers' wages, it feels like they're getting a pay cut. Companies, meanwhile, benefit.

item.title: State Farm is sending refund checks to customers. Here's who qualifies.
item.description: More than 7.2 million checks have been mailed so far, with millions more expected to go out this week, according to State Farm.

item.title: U.S. deporting Mexican migrants to Guatemala and Honduras, angering Mexico
item.description: The Trump administration has been quietly deporting migrants from Mexico to Central America, despite the Mexican government's willingness to accept the return of all its citizens.

item.title: Penn State frat brothers charged with running cocaine trafficking ring
item.description: Two Penn State fraternities are at the center of a cocaine trafficking ring bust, leading to charges against 14 people, authorities said.

item.title: IRS proposal would force nonprofits to disclose leaders' terrorism convictions
item.description: The disclosure requirement would be added to the Form 990, the annual return that nonprofit groups file with the IRS.

item.title: Tupac Shakur was murdered in "act of revenge," prosecutor tells jury
item.description: The long-unsolved drive-by shooting gripped the hip-hop community, partly because no one was charged until Duane "Keffe D" Davis was indicted in 2023.

item.title: Extended interview: Rachel Goldberg-Polin on grief after the death of her son, Hersh
item.description: Anderson Cooper spoke with Rachel Goldberg-Polin, an American Israeli mother whose son, Hersh, was kidnapped by Hamas on Oct. 7, 2023 and then executed. Editor's note: The video above is an extended version of the interview that was broadcast on 60 Minutes on Sunday, April 19, 2026. This extended version was condensed for clarity.

item.title: Stewart Copeland turns his studio into a wild orchestra
item.description: The Police drummer gives Bill Whitaker a tour of his Los Angeles studio, where custom percussion, rare instruments, and nature-inspired sounds come together in his latest project, "Wild Concerto."

item.title: Boston's Big Dig | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: In 1997, Lesley Stahl reported on Boston's road project, known as the Big Dig, meant to alleviate a perpetual traffic jam downtown. The seven-and-a-half mile, $10 billion stretch of highway remains the most expensive highway project in U.S. history.

item.title: ZZ Top is "Goin' 50"
item.description: The band ZZ Top is marking 50 years together, with a new remastered collection of their greatest hits, "Goin' 50." Jim Axlerod talks with guitarist Billy Gibbons, bassist Dusty Hill, and drummer Frank Beard (the one without a beard) who are still working hard to make their pedal-to-the-metal, bluesy country rock seem so easy.
